scope: confirm the reliable-command wire format used by the CODOL build

codol_wire_constants.comment: both builds use service 1 for sequence + NUL-terminated text; retail service 2 is a distinct binary command (sequence + u16 length + bytes)

write_order: if n: MSG_WriteShort(msg, n) + MSG_WriteData(payload, n)
verified_facts.therefore: each reliable command on the wire is opcode(1) + sequence(4) + either a NUL-terminated string or u16 length + bytes

confront_with_capture.expected_at_body_start: opcode should be 1 (text) or 2 (binary), then a 4-byte sequence
confront_with_capture.observed_at_offset_10: 03 00 00 00 00 - neither opcode 1/2 nor a plausible sequence
confront_with_capture.conclusion: the real opcode and sequence sit inside the ten contaminated bytes, so the 03 at offset 10 is something else (likely part of the command payload), not the reliable-command header

next: solve the first ten bytes using the known header shape: plaintext must start with opcode(1)=01 or 02, then a small sequence (1..100)
with the correct opcode/seq assumption, solve for the command string that produces the observed key shift
